title: A Consequence-Based Response Framework for a More Resilient Shipping Amidst Growing Uncertainty
content: The 2011 Fukushima disaster,  the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020  are two, least expected and highly disruptive, events about ten years apart. Both had an immediate impact, but also longer-term repercussions on shipping business operations.  However, while pandemics are a recurrent phenomenon of the known-known type, the combination of phenomena which led to Fukushima had no assigned probability. Hence no preparedness was in place as this was a practically  unique occurrence in shipping. Considering significant shipping incidents of various less uncommon etiologies also, as are missile attacks on merchant  ships or vessel-onto-bridge  collisions,  the paper puts forward a different  general framework for handling  shocks in the maritime domain, especially the ones classified in the “unknown-unknown” or “Black Swan” category, proposing a consequence-based approach. A parallel  to other approaches and tools emphasis by shipping businesses on the  Assessment-reaction-Recovery-Conversion (ArRC) framework for managing risk may assist in  a) increasing resilience through planning for consequence-oriented, root-neutral reactions and b) promoting a “bounce-back-better”  frame of mind, contributing to  faster and easier  recovery after a  shock of any type.
